ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Ammonia is the best-known nitrogen-hydrogen compound; however, there are a number of other nitrogen-hydrogen compounds, three of which are in the above diagram. Which of these has the longest average N-N bond length?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Graph description: The figure lists three nitrogen-hydrogen compounds: Diazene is shown as H-N=N-H, with only one N-N double bond; Triazene is shown as H-N≡N-NH2, containing one N≡N triple bond and one N-N single bond; Tetrazene is shown as H2N-N=N-NH2, containing two N-N single bonds and one N=N double bond. Reasoning: Calculate the N-N bond order according to the number of connecting lines. The average N-N bond order of Diazene is 2; the average N-N bond order of Triazene is (3+1)/2 = 2; the average N-N bond order of Tetrazene is (1+2+1)/3 = 4/3. N-N bond length increases as bond order decreases, so Tetrazene, which has the smallest average bond order, has the longest average N-N bond length, and its molecular formula is N4H4.

raw_record.question_text: Among the nitrogen-hydrogen compounds shown in the above diagram, which one has the longest average N-N bond length?

method.method_draft: Identify each compound in the image and count the order of every N–N bond shown by the number of connecting lines. Compute the average N–N bond order for each molecule. Since N–N bond length increases as bond order decreases, select the compound with the smallest average N–N bond order. This gives tetrazene, formula N4H4, as having the longest average N–N bond length.
